<b>Лобная кость</b> — лоб и верхние края: Frontal bone — the forehead and upper rims of the orbits; its orbital plates form the orbital roofs. Above the bridge of the nose it contains the frontal sinus. At birth the bone is in two halves; the suture between them (metopic) usually closes by 1–2 years.
<b>Теменные кости</b> — парные, образуют: Parietal bones — paired, they form most of the cranial vault. They meet each other at the sagittal suture, the frontal bone at the coronal, the occipital at the lambdoid and the temporal at the squamous suture.
<b>Затылочная кость</b> — задняя часть с: Occipital bone — the back of the vault and of the base. It contains the foramen magnum, where the medulla oblongata becomes the spinal cord. On each side of the foramen the condyles articulate with the first cervical vertebra (atlas) — the nodding joint.
Temporal bones — at the sides of the skull. Their petrous parts hide the middle and inner ear; outside are the external acoustic meatus, the mastoid process behind it and, in front, the zygomatic process and the fossa for the mandible.
<b>Клиновидная кость</b> похожа на бабоч: Sphenoid bone is shaped like a butterfly and sits in the middle of the base, meeting every bone of the neurocranium. Its body holds the sella turcica with the pituitary and the sphenoid sinus; the greater wings show at the temples and deep in the orbits, the pterygoid processes from below.
<b>Решётчатая кость</b> — лёгкая кость м: Ethmoid bone — a light bone between the orbits. Its cribriform plate lets olfactory nerve fibers pass from the nose to the brain, its perpendicular plate forms the upper nasal septum, and its air-cell labyrinth forms orbital walls and the superior and middle nasal conchae.
<b>Носовые кости</b> — две маленькие пла: Nasal bones — two small plates that form the bridge of the nose. They are the most often fractured facial bones.
<b>Слёзные кости</b> — самые маленькие к: Lacrimal bones — the smallest facial bones, thin plates at the front of the medial orbital wall. Their fossa holds the lacrimal sac, from which tears drain down the nasolacrimal canal into the nose.
<b>Скуловые кости</b> формируют скулы и: Zygomatic bones form the cheekbones and the lateral rims of the orbits; with the zygomatic process of the temporal bone they make the zygomatic arch, where the masseter muscle begins.
<b>Верхняя челюсть</b> — парная кость: д: Maxilla — a paired bone: floor of the orbit, walls of the nose, the front ¾ of the hard palate and the alveolar process with the upper teeth. Inside is the largest sinus, the maxillary sinus.
<b>Нёбные кости</b> — L-образные пластин: Palatine bones — L-shaped plates behind the maxillae: their horizontal plates form the back of the hard palate, their vertical plates part of the nasal wall. Best seen from below.
<b>Сошник</b> — непарная пластинка в глу: Vomer — an unpaired plate deep in the nose: the lower and back part of the nasal septum. The ethmoid joins it above, the septal cartilage in front.
<b>Нижние носовые раковины</b> — самосто: Inferior nasal conchae — separate scrolls on the side walls of the nose (the superior and middle conchae belong to the ethmoid). Covered with mucosa, they warm and moisten inhaled air.
<b>Нижняя челюсть</b> — единственная под: Mandible — the only movable bone of the skull. Its condyles form the two temporomandibular joints with the temporal bones, which always work together: when the mouth opens wide, the condyle glides forward onto the articular tubercle.
<b>Большое затылочное отверстие</b> — са: Foramen magnum — the largest opening. Here the medulla oblongata becomes the spinal cord; the vertebral arteries and the spinal roots of the accessory nerve (XI) pass alongside. Its rim lies in the occipital bone.
<b>Подъязычный канал</b> — над мыщелком: Hypoglossal canal — above the occipital condyle. The hypoglossal nerve (XII), the motor nerve of the tongue, leaves through it.
<b>Яремное отверстие</b> — между затылоч: Jugular foramen — between the occipital and temporal bones. The internal jugular vein (draining blood from the brain) leaves through it, with three cranial nerves: glossopharyngeal (IX), vagus (X) and accessory (XI).
<b>Сонный канал</b> — в пирамиде височно: Carotid canal — in the petrous temporal bone. The internal carotid artery bends through it into the cranial cavity to supply the brain.
<b>Шилососцевидное отверстие</b> — между: Stylomastoid foramen — between the styloid and mastoid processes. The facial nerve (VII) exits here to the muscles of facial expression; when it is inflamed, half of the face droops (Bell’s palsy).
<b>Овальное отверстие</b> — в большом кр: Foramen ovale — in the greater wing of the sphenoid. The third division of the trigeminal nerve (V₃) passes through it to the chewing muscles, the lower teeth and the skin of the chin.
<b>Остистое отверстие</b> — маленькое, п: Foramen spinosum — small, behind the foramen ovale. The middle meningeal artery enters the skull through it; its tear after a blow to the temple causes a dangerous epidural hematoma.
<b>Рваное отверстие</b> — щель между пир: Foramen lacerum — a gap between the petrous temporal, occipital and sphenoid bones. In life it is closed by cartilage; the internal carotid artery runs across its upper surface.
<b>Большое нёбное отверстие</b> — в задн: Greater palatine foramen — at the back corner of the hard palate. The greater palatine nerve and vessels emerge here to the palatal mucosa; dentists inject anesthetic at this spot.
<b>Резцовое отверстие</b> — позади верхн: Incisive foramen — behind the upper incisors, in the midline of the palate. The nasopalatine nerve passes through it to the mucosa of the front of the palate.
<b>Передний (большой) родничок</b> — ром: Anterior (large) fontanelle — a diamond where the frontal and both parietal bones meet, about 2–3 cm across. The largest; it closes by 1–2 years. Doctors use it to judge intracranial pressure and dehydration: it sinks when the baby lacks fluid.
<b>Задний (малый) родничок</b> — треугол: Posterior (small) fontanelle — a triangle between the parietal and occipital bones. It closes early, by 2–3 months (in many babies it is almost closed at birth).
<b>Клиновидный родничок</b> — сбоку, где: Sphenoidal fontanelle — at the side, where the frontal, parietal, temporal and sphenoid bones meet (in adults this spot is called the pterion). It closes at about 6 months.
<b>Сосцевидный родничок</b> — сзади-сбок: Mastoid fontanelle — at the back of the side, where the parietal, occipital and temporal bones meet (the asterion). It closes by 6–18 months.
<b>Череп</b> — 22 кости (без слуховых ко: Skull — 22 bones (not counting the ear ossicles): 8 form the neurocranium, 14 the face. All except the mandible are joined by immovable sutures. Click a bone or pick it below.
<b>Основание черепа снизу</b> (нижняя че: Skull base from below (mandible removed). The spinal cord, the brain’s blood vessels and the cranial nerves pass through the openings of the base. Pick an opening to see what goes through it.
<b>Череп новорождённого</b>: лицо малень: Newborn skull: the face is small — about 1/8 of the skull (≈ 1/2 in adults) — and the vault bones have not yet fused. Between them are soft membranes, the fontanelles: during birth the bones can overlap slightly, and later the brain grows fast.
Двадцать две кости, сросшиеся швами в пр: Twenty-two bones joined by sutures into a sturdy case for the brain and a frame for the face. We take them one by one, look at the openings in the skull base and at a newborn’s skull.
\n <div><h2>Строение</h2>\n:
Structure

Neurocranium (8 bones): frontal, two parietal, occipital, two temporal, sphenoid, ethmoid. Face (14): two maxillae, the mandible, two zygomatic, two nasal, two lacrimal, two palatine, two inferior nasal conchae, the vomer. The hyoid and the ear ossicles are usually counted separately.

Sutures

Coronal (frontal–parietals), sagittal (between the parietals), lambdoid (parietals–occipital), squamous (temporal–parietal). The spot where the frontal, parietal, temporal and sphenoid bones meet is the pterion: the bone is thin here and the middle meningeal artery runs beneath it.

Base

From inside, the base is divided into the anterior, middle and posterior cranial fossae (for the frontal lobes, the temporal lobes, the cerebellum and brainstem). Besides the openings seen from below there are inner ones: the optic canal (nerve II), superior orbital fissure (III, IV, V₁, VI), foramen rotundum (V₂), internal acoustic meatus (VII, VIII).

Medicine

A basal skull fracture betrays itself by “raccoon eyes” and clear fluid (CSF) leaking from the nose or ear. Premature fusion of sutures in a child (craniosynostosis) deforms the head and is corrected surgically. A blow to the temple is dangerous because it can tear the middle meningeal artery.

Simplifications

  • The bones are colored on a real 3D skeleton model; the borders between them are drawn by landmarks and smoothed, so the sutures are approximate. The model has no ear ossicles and no inner walls of the cranial fossae.
  • The openings of the base are marked by dots at their approximate places; not all of them are visible as holes on the model. The ethmoid, vomer and conchae deep in the nose are simplified.
  • The newborn skull is made from the adult one: the face and jaws are smoothly shrunk and the fontanelles are drawn over the vault. A real baby has no visible teeth (they are hidden in the jaws), no mastoid process, and thinner vault bones separated by wide membranes.
